links.note: Was 24037 Ethnic group. The question asks the nationality of the artist Frederic Sorrieu, who painted the Democratic and Social Republic - that is 'The Rise of Nationalism in Europe' (chapter 23705), and it is item 1 of the mixed sample paper whose items 2-30 landed on this chapter unlinked. Nothing in Power Sharing's 17 concepts concerns a European artist or his painting.

Was 24040 Regional concentration. The question asks India's territorial water limit, which is Geography (Resources and Development, chapter 23693). 24040 is about Belgium's and Sri Lanka's communities being concentrated in different regions; it shares only the word 'territorial'. Item 10 of the same misfiled sample paper.

Was 24052 Vertical sharing among levels. The question asks which country has a federal form of government - the concept it tests is Federalism's 'Federal system' (24058 in chapter 23711), where I have linked the identical stem at qid:105427. This chapter's 24052 defines vertical sharing but never classifies countries as federal or unitary. Item 21 of the same misfiled sample paper, whose siblings qid:105362/105363/105365 I left unlinked for the same reason.

Was 24041 Tension in Brussels. The question is 'What is the capital city of France?' - general geography, not Class 10 Civics at all. It matched 24041 only because that concept's text mentions French speakers. No concept in this chapter's closed set covers it, and the row looks like a stray.
